digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate impact model calibration and criteria
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings and was never calibrated post-inception, leaving ~90% of omitted-scope findings graded as none despite constituting a real class of plan divergence

A G6 finding (c4ad-a93e-0613-408f) correctly identified a plan flaw but scored impact=0.0 and landed advisory rather than blocking because all seven impact axes graded none, revealing that divergent_implementation must distinguish load-bearing divergences (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site) from cosmetic ones (incomplete_enumeration)

The divergent_implementation axis must migrate from ordinal grades (none|low|medium|high) to a closed Literal set with floors at 0.85 for blocking grades and incomplete_enumeration mapped below all blocking thresholds, mirroring the established ac_unverifiable oracle-kind pattern

A proposed prod_impact floor was rejected because it would remove 1.9x more convergence headroom than the divergence fix by lifting an unbounded severity class orthogonal to whether findings are novel, violating the rising-floor convergence termination guarantee

ADR 0054 must reject purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review as calibration instruments, narrowing ADR 0036's A/B clause to only corpus replay and dogfood observation — both zero-marginal-cost forms

Impact model version must bump from plan-v3 to plan-v4 with structural changes to impact_plan: exclude divergent_implementation from _SEV01 contribution, add DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 mapping, introduce _PLAN_GRADED_AXES for unified axis handling, and update both verifier prompts and G7 prompt-side consumers with explicit grade definitions
